subject: Re: Go-to-close plan / MAP, evaluation milestones & commercial redlines
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finservai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finservai.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot MAP & evaluation timing — initial inputs

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked promising for our recommender use case. Procurement has asked me to share an initial outline of what we need from a go-to-close plan so we can align internal stakeholders. High-level asks: 

- A 6–8 week evaluation window with a clear acceptance checklist (latency, P95 < 120ms; 99th < 300ms; embedding drift <= 2% vs baseline).
- A milestone-driven MAP with pay-as-you-go credits during the pilot and an option to convert to a committed monthly reservation at the end of the pilot.
- Clarity on how "usage" is defined (inference tokens vs embedding compute vs request count) and how true-ups/true-downs are applied after conversion.
- Price protection terms for the first 12 months post-conversion.
- Any data residency / audit log evidence we can provide for our security team.

I've attached our RFP and a short procurement checklist (FinServAI_RFP.pdf). We're going to run this through legal/procurement but wanted to get your commercial team to propose a MAP and the pricing mechanics that will govern the pilot -> committed conversion.

Can you share a draft MAP and a short commercial summary by next Tue (11/2)?

—Alex
Director, AI Platforms
FinServAI

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finservai.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & evaluation timing — initial inputs

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. We're aligned on the checklist items and can absolutely produce the artifact you need. Attaching a first-cut MAP workbook (MAP_v1.xlsx) and a one-pager commercial summary. Key points up-front:

- Evaluation window: 6 weeks (2-week sandbox + 4-week benchmark). Acceptance gated on the checklist you shared.
- Pilot economics: $0.00 up to 50k tokens/day in week 1–2 (sandbox), then billed at eval rates with a credit bucket of $15k for evaluation usage.
- Conversion options: 3-tier commitment (S: 500k/mo, M: 2.5M/mo, L: 8M/mo) with stepped discounts at each tier (7% / 12% / 20%).
- True-up cadence: Quarterly true-ups against committed units for the first 12 months; we proposed a 60-day true-up window after quarter close.
- Price protection: prices guaranteed for 12 months from conversion date.

Questions we have: how flexible do you need the commit sizing (we can do calendar-quarter or a 90-day rolling window), and can procurement accept quarterly true-ups or do they require monthly reconciliation?

Next steps: Priyom will own the commercial follow-up and v1 redlines; I'll coordinate a short MAP review workshop end of next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finservai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & evaluation timing — initial inputs

Alex / Vanessa — looping in Karthik (commercial/legal partner) since a couple of the terms will be in the contract and we want to surface tradeoffs early. A few clarifications from my side after reviewing MAP_v1:

1) True-up mechanics: our standard is quarterly true-ups for the first 12 months when customers are on a commit. That gives both sides time to normalize usage patterns on a seasonal / product launch cadence. If Procurement requires monthly reconciliations we can provide monthly statements but we prefer to keep financial settlements quarterly to limit churn.

2) Definition of usage: we need to agree primary metering signals. Proposal: bill on "billable tokens" (inference + prompt tokens) with embeddings billed as a per-embedding-unit addendum (separate SKU). We should define a single canonical metric in the contract to avoid disputes — e.g., "billable token equivalent (BTE)" with conversion ratios for embeddings.

3) Price protection: we can offer a 12-month price hold post-conversion. However, customers who significantly exceed committed bands (e.g., >200% of commitment in a quarter) may trigger a review and potential rate adjustment for incremental usage. We can soften that by adding an upper-bound rate cap for incremental overage during the first year.

I've attached a short outline of suggested contract language and SLA redlines (SLA_redlines_v1.docx) for Karthik to review. Karthik — can you share recommended language around BTE and the true-up waterfall?

—Priyom
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finservai.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & evaluation timing — initial inputs

Priyom / Team — quick legal/commercial notes below (high-level, not final redlines):

- Usage definition: propose the contract define two metering buckets: "Generation Tokens" (prompt + response) and "Embedding Units" (per-embedding request), with conversion ratios spelled out in Schedule A. Example language: "Billable Units = Generation Tokens + (Embedding Units * 0.5)" — the 0.5 multiplier is negotiable but gives both teams a clear reconciliation path.

- True-up waterfall: (1) Monthly usage reporting; (2) Quarterly invoicing and settlement for delta vs commit (i.e., if aggregated quarterly usage < commit, customer receives a credit; if > commit, customer pays overage per agreed incremental rates). For the pilot → conversion, propose a 90-day staged true-up (30/60/90 days) to allow smoothing of onboarding spikes.

- Price protection: offer 12 months price protection on committed rates. For incremental overage we suggest a 6-month capped price increase on incremental bands (not exceeding X% without mutual consent). Recommend we replace vague "review" language with explicit caps.

- Audit & logs: we can provide a monthly CSV export of request-level logs and a SOC2 attestation; any additional audit effort (on-site or deep-dive) can be scoped as professional services.

I'll mark up the draft contract with concrete wording; attaching SLA_redlines_v1.docx for reference. If FinServAI prefers monthly settlement we can support it but will need to amend the MAP economics (higher handling fee / smaller discounts).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Commercial Counsel | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SLA_redlines_v1.docx)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finservai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finservai.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 13:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & evaluation timing — initial inputs

Vanessa / Priyom / Karthik — appreciate the fast turn. A few procurement/legal asks from our side after internal review: 

- Procurement is pushing back on quarterly settlement. Their org needs monthly invoicing and reconciliation for budget control. They will accept quarterly true-up if we can guarantee net terms of 30 days and provide a monthly statement within 10 business days of month-end.

- Price protection: they want the 12-month protection extended to the entire platform rates (including overage bands) until the customer anniversary, not just committed tier. That's a heavier ask — can Redwood accept that?

- True-up cadence: the staged 90-day true-up is acceptable but they want the first stage (30 days) to trigger a preliminary estimate invoice so they can plan cash flow.

- Usage definitions: our engineering team says they will not accept multipliers in Schedule A without an auditable mapping. They want per-endpoint meter definitions (e.g., /generate uses tokens A–Z; /embed uses 1 embedding unit per call) and a sample conversion table.

I've attached Procurement_COMMENTS.docx with markup. We can be flexible on discounts if you can tighten up the true-up timing and provide a monthly usage statement.

—Alex
Director, AI Platforms
FinServAI
(Attachment: Procurement_COMMENTS.docx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finservai.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & evaluation timing — initial inputs

Alex — thanks, all good and appreciated content. Quick summary and compromise proposal so we can move to signatures: 

1) Monthly statements + 30-day net terms: yes — we will provide a monthly usage statement within 7 business days of month-end (we can tighten to 7), and standard 30-day net terms on invoices. Monthly invoicing is fine; operational handling fee will be absorbed for the pilot period (no extra fee during evaluation).

2) Staged true-up: accept the 90-day staged approach, but we will issue a preliminary estimate invoice at 30 days (non-final) and an interim settlement at 60 days, final settlement at 90 days. Final settlement language will note that the 30/60 invoices are estimates and that the 90-day invoice is binding.

3) Price protection: we can extend price protection for 12 months on committed tier pricing. For incremental overage bands, we will cap increases at 10% for the first 12 months post-conversion (i.e., incremental unit rate will not increase >10% without mutual written consent).

4) Usage definitions & billing meter: we'll replace the ad-hoc multiplier with a Schedule A table that lists per-endpoint metering and conversion ratios and provide sample CSV mappings from your environment during the pilot so you can validate.

5) MAP & next steps: attaching an updated MAP for signature (MAP_final_for_signature.xlsx) and a Commercial_Summary.pdf. If this direction is acceptable, can FinServAI sign the MAP and return by Tue 11/9 so we can begin sandbox provisioning 11/16 and start evaluation week of 11/23?

I'll set up a 30-min review call for Mon 11/8 to walk legal/procurement through the Schedule A mapping and the 30/60/90 invoicing flow.

Thanks — look forward to closing.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
